subject: Control-plane partitioning narrative for SOC 2 / SIG — condensed diagrams and reconciled claims
messages:
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@veridian.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Audit Team <audit@veridian.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: condensed control-plane partition narrative & diagram

Hi Rafael / Kimberly,

As part of Verdant's SOC 2 examiner review we need a concise narrative (one page max) describing how Redwood partitions the control plane between hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments, plus a small annotated diagram (single page PDF) that shows the partition boundaries and allowed interconnects for Dedicated vs Private. The examiner specifically asked for:

- A short description of the control-plane components and which are customer-managed vs Redwood-managed.
- The data paths for configuration updates, secrets provisioning (KMS/HSM calls), and audit log export.
- Failover behavior and how we prevent cross-tenant leakage when routing control plane requests.

Can you provide a single-page narrative + a diagram and a simple CSV table that maps each control-plane endpoint to its trust boundary (internal, VPC peered, customer-managed)? We don't need deep network diagrams — the request is for a reconciled claim set that the auditor can reference in their SOC 2 / SIG report.

Timing: if possible, please send by EOD today Pacific — the examiner is on a tight schedule.

Thanks,
Sara Jenkins
Cloud Security Lead, Verdant Systems
Sara.Jenkins@veridian.com

--
Attachment: none (initial request)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@veridian.com>, Audit Team <audit@veridian.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: condensed control-plane partition narrative & diagram

Kimberly / team — looping you in to produce a concise deliverable for Verdant. I put together a one-page narrative and a single-sheet diagram (mini) plus a CSV that maps endpoints to trust boundaries. Attachments are: control-plane-partitioning-mini-diagram.pdf and segmentation-claim-table.csv.

High-level summary (for the auditor):
- Control plane components: config-api (Redwood-managed), routing/orchestration controller (Redwood-managed), customer-delegated control agent (runs in customer VPC for Private), and metrics/telemetry export endpoints (Redwood-managed but with configurable retention).
- Customer-managed pieces (Private): control agent, KMS integration endpoints (customer keywrap), and optional on-prem audit log forwarder.
- Interconnects: Private deployments use customer VPC peering or dedicated interconnect; Dedicated uses a reserved network segment within Redwood with tenant isolation and enforced egress controls.
- Secrets & KMS: Customers can bring keys; Redwood never persists unwrapped keys. KMS calls traverse an authenticated control channel with mutual TLS; diagram annotates the handshake.
- Failover: Router-level fallbacks are strictly per-tenant; KV caches and prefix caches are keyed with tenant IDs and are never replicated outside the tenant's zone.

Deliverables attached. Notes on scope / limitations are in the narrative footnote. If the auditor wants more granularity on port-level allowances or switch-level zoning we should route to infra, but Verdant asked for a reconciled claim set not a full topology.

Rafael Mendes
Head of Applied Security, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Attachments: control-plane-partitioning-mini-diagram.pdf (PDF, 1pg), segmentation-claim-table.csv (CSV, 1 sheet)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@veridian.com>, Audit Team <audit@veridian.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: condensed control-plane partition narrative & diagram

Sara — sending along Rafael's consolidated packet (attached). Quick clarification from our side:

- The "customer-delegated control agent" referenced in the narrative runs in the customer's VPC for Private deployments; for Dedicated we run an agent in the reserved Redwood segment but with per-tenant keys and strictly scoped control APIs.
- For KMS calls: when customers bring their own keys we perform an encrypted key-wrap; the CSV maps the KMS calls and whether the wrapped key is persisted.

I've also added a single reference link (internal redwood drive) with the annotated SVG version of the diagram for your reviewer to zoom in if needed: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ExampleMiniDiag

If the examiner needs a signed attestation from infra about switch-level zoning, say the word and I'll pull Marcus / Michael into the thread. Otherwise this should satisfy the reconciled claims request.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security Architecture, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

1) Would you add a single-line note in the narrative that states explicitly "No unwrapped customer keys are stored by Redwood" (this is a direct auditor prompt).
2) In the CSV could you add a column mapping the control-plane endpoint to the SOC 2 control (e.g., CC6.1, CC7.2) where applicable — just a best-effort mapping.

If you can push an updated narrative + CSV by tomorrow morning PST that would be ideal. Otherwise we can proceed with what you sent and raise a small follow-up in the report.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Verdant's auditor is on a tight timeline.

Sara Jenkins
